name: Salmar

claims.text:
The Gnomish cognate of Salmar is Salvor.
Likewise, both Noldorin and Lirillo (another name by which he was known by) are also Qenya names: the first probably arising from his association with the Noldoli; the second meaning "Valu of the Song", containing either glîr ("a song, poem") or lir- ("sing") + masculine ending -illo.
The Gnomish equivalent of Noldorin is Goldriel, and that of Lirillo is Glirlos.
Another name for the character was Avlon. It is in Gnomish, but its meaning is unclear.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Early Qenya and The Valmaric Script", in Parma Eldalamberon XIV (edited by Carl F. Hostetter, Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, Patrick H. Wynne, and Bill Welden), p. 13; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "I. The Cottage of Lost Play": "Notes and Commentary", p. 22; J.R.R. Tolkien, "I-Lam na-Ngoldathon: The Grammar and Lexicon of the Gnomish Tongue", in Parma Eldalamberon XI (edited by Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, and Patrick H. Wynne), p. 41

claims.text: Salmar is a Qenya name, derived from salma ("lyre, small harp").
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Early Qenya and The Valmaric Script", in Parma Eldalamberon XIV (edited by Carl F. Hostetter, Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, Patrick H. Wynne, and Bill Welden), p. 13

claims.text: He entered the world with Ulmo, and afterwards dwelt in Valmar. There he would often play music on his harp and lyre, sitting beneath Laurelin, and Ómar-Amillo his twin brother would sing as he played.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "III. The Coming of the Valar and the Building of Valinor", p. 66; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "III. The Coming of the Valar and the Building of Valinor", p. 75
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > The Book of Lost Tales and associated writings

claims.text: When the Valar decided to oust Melko from his fortress in Utumna, he joined the rest of them in their attack. Some time later when the Elves awoke, he established a friendship with the Noldoli, whom he loved.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "IV. The Chaining of Melko", p. 101; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "V. The Coming of the Elves and the Making of Kôr", p. 126
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > The Book of Lost Tales and associated writings

claims.text: After the Two Trees were destroyed, it was Salmar who first noticed that in Vána's lamentation for them, there was still joy in her voice. When he pointed it out to them, the rest of the Valar gathered there heard the words: I-kal'antúlien (meaning "Light hath returned"), since Vána's tears caused a final shoot of Laurelin to spring forth.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "VIII. The Tale of the Sun and Moon", p. 184
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > The Book of Lost Tales and associated writings

claims.text: Much later, after the Fall of Gondolin, when the Valar finally decided to wage war on Melko in the Great Lands and free the enslaved Gnomes, Salmar came with them. In the ensuing Battle of Tasarinan, Salmar barely escaped; following his escape he went to the Iron Mountains looking for the Gnomes and to find their place of imprisonment.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "III. The Fall of Gondolin", p. 154; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "VI. The History of Eriol or Ælfwine and the End of the Tales", p. 279
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > The Book of Lost Tales and associated writings

claims.text: Nothing else is known about his future, except that he eventually returned to Valinor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "VI. The History of Eriol or Ælfwine and the End of the Tales", p. 278; J.R.R. Tolkien, "Qenyaqetsa: The Qenya Phonology and Lexicon", in Parma Eldalamberon XII (edited by Carl F. Hostetter, Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, and Patrick H. Wynne), p. 36; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "III. The Fall of Gondolin": "Notes and Commentary", pp. 219-220
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > The Book of Lost Tales and associated writings

claims.text: In one text though, it is said that he led the Gnomes back to Tol Eressëa after the war with Melko.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Qenyaqetsa: The Qenya Phonology and Lexicon", in Parma Eldalamberon XII (edited by Carl F. Hostetter, Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, and Patrick H. Wynne), p. 67
